chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hadrami [al-Husayn] [al-Husayn] narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd [Yazid], from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family):

He said: The Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him) died suddenly on a Saturday, so the birds shaded him with their wings. Musa, the Word of Allah, died in the wilderness, so a caller cried out from the sky: 'Musa has died! And which soul does not die!'

key_terms.كَلِيمُ اللَّهِ: The Word of Allah (a title for Prophet Musa)
key_terms.وَأَيُّ نَفْسٍ لَا تَمُوتُ: And which soul does not die (rhetorical affirmation of inevitability)

ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet Dawud and Prophet Musa died according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt chain in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, vividly illustrates the universality of death (*al-mawt*) by contrasting the peaceful, nature-assisted passing of Prophet Dawud with the dramatic, celestial announcement accompanying Prophet Musa’s death in the wilderness. It serves as a powerful memento mori, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the inevitability of death as a divine decree that applies even to the highest prophets, thereby encouraging spiritual preparation and humility.
